rule.description: The User account record's field set (id, email, password) is declared exactly once, by the persistence module that creates and queries the table (the module containing pgTable('User', {...})). A function declared outside that owner module that makes two or more member accesses to those record fields in its body keeps reaching around the owner: it is more interested in the User record than in the responsibility of the module it lives in, so the record-level behavior is misplaced and belongs with the owner. A single field access is ordinary data use and does not count.

owner_definition.owner_exemption_rationale: The owner module is exempt from the rule: functions inside the persistence module accessing their own record's fields is exactly the data locality the repair restores.

checks.description: Detect functions outside the User-record owner module that dissect User-record fields (id, email, password) two or more times, doing the record's work away from the module that declares and persists the record.
checks.detected_relation: non-owner function -> repeated member access on User-record fields owned by app/db.ts
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Feature envy: each flagged function primarily operates on the account record's data instead of the responsibility of the module it lives in, so the record's rules live spread across presentation and auth wiring instead of with their owner.

matches.evidence: function 'isExistingAccount' (line 49) makes 2 accesses to User-record field(s) email,password at line(s) 53,54; the signup screen re-validates fetched rows field by field (existing.email === email, !!existing.password) to decide whether an account already exists.

method 'authorize' (line 16) makes 3 accesses to User-record field(s) password,email at line(s) 20,20,21; the credentials callback gates the stored-hash comparison on the record's own fields (record.password && record.email) before comparing and returning the record.

function 'greetingFor' (line 19) makes 5 accesses to User-record field(s) email,id at line(s) 21,21,22,22,23; the dashboard greeting is derived by stepping through the stored account's identity fields (user.email, user.id, session?.user?.email) instead of delegating identity to the record's owner.

excluded.subject: app/db.ts (all functions, including getUser, createUser, and any account-level helpers added by a repair)
excluded.reason: Owner module: it declares the pgTable('User', {...}) mapping and persists the record, so its own record accesses are the desired data locality, not envy.

excluded.subject: single field accesses below the two-access threshold, e.g. the clean state's session?.user?.email render and the clean state's single user[0].password comparison
excluded.reason: Ordinary data use at module boundaries; the rule requires repeated dissection of record internals, not one legitimate read.

excluded.subject: app/auth.config.ts authorized callback reading auth?.user to decide route protection
excluded.reason: Session and routing state are that callback's own responsibility, and the module must stay importable from the Edge middleware runtime; inspecting session state there is not record envy.

excluded.subject: presentation components (app/form.tsx, app/submit-button.tsx) and route wiring (middleware.ts, app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts)
excluded.reason: No user-record data is in scope; props and route configuration are those modules' own data.
